MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ADJOURNED MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 19, 2022

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 6:02 p.m. at City of Rolling Hills Estates Council Chambers,
  4045 Palos Verdes Dr. N., Rolling Hills Estates, California, Pepperwood Park and Peter
  Weber Equestrian Center (Park Tours) by CHAIR CIAROLLA.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR CIAROLLA led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Pope,  Ciarolla,  Persichina,  Romanelli,
  McCormick, and Retz

  Commissioners Absent:  Bain

  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrow

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF August 15,
  2022

  COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by
  COMMISSIONER POPE to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  August 15, 2022.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
September 19, 2022
   A.  CITY CELEBRATION UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the City
  Celebration event held at the Empty Saddle Club on Saturday, September 17. She
  offered a thank you to the commissioners who volunteered at the event. She also
  reported that the event went great with wonderful weather throughout the day. She
  stated that there appeared to be a smaller attendance compared to last year
  possibly due to another event in the area, but that there was a steady stream of
  participants throughout the day. She also informed the group that the City
  conducted a pre-sale of wristbands for the event activities resulting in 38 wristbands
  sold. She then stated that the City was also able to accept credit cards at the event
  with 39 transactions completed. She informed the Commission that she would
  present more details with an informational report after the subcommittee holds their
  debrief meeting.

  B.  2022 HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE DEBRIEF

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of the written
  report.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated a friend who participated in race had some
  feedback that she would share with staff since she was unable to send it prior to
  the subcommittee debrief. Community Services Supervisor noted that it would still
  be beneficial to assist in prepping for next year’s race.

  COMMISSION POPE also stated that the tunnel seemed very dark and proposed
  looking into placing temporary lights inside.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA stated that he went to the website of the 5k race
  that took place on Sunday 9/18 [Strides for Recovery 5k] and noted that the website
  stated that the race was sold out and asked how many participants were there.
  ACM Davis stated that it appeared that they had around 200-300 participants but
  explained that they did use a race promoter and chip timers. COMMISSIONER
  PERSICHINA stated that costs involved for a race promoter last time they
  researched were up to $4,000 for a promoter, with 50% of the sponsor money to
  the promoter and 50% of entry fees. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI also stated
  that we have done a couple of races successfully on our own and discourages the
  use of a promoter. He stated that through our own efforts, we were able to give
  $6,000 to the Pepper Tree Foundation with this year’s race where that may have
  been different if utilizing a promoter. CHAIR CIAROLLA stated that we could use
  the DJ from the City Celebration. ACM Davis noted that we have investigated that.
  ACM Davis also noted that the feedback we heard was that it was the race had light
  attendance. She explained that staff could research different type of promoters with
  the goal of bringing in more participants rather than sponsors to make it more of a

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
September 19, 2022
   cost recovery than an added expense and bring that information back to the
  subcommittee and Commission for a future decision. COMMISSIONER
  ROMANELLI agreed that this was a fair assessment and appreciates the effort to
  conduct the research.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if this was the event that typically has a lot
  of remaining t-shirts and other supplies. ACM Davis and Community Services
  Supervisor Pinuelas note that measures were taken this year to not order as many
  shirts and other supplies as in past years to help reduce costs.

  COMMISSIONER POPE noted that she agreed with COMMISSIONER
  ROMANELLI that we may not need a full level promoter for this event and to not
  have that level of expense. She also noted that it may be better to look into the chip
  timers as the feedback in the past has indicated a desire for that item. CHAIR
  CIAROLLA agrees that chip timers may be beneficial as runners do like to know
  their times. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas shared that the cost was
  around $2,500 for chip timers in last year’s research.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ noted that if the City went with another promoter that the
  City should be guaranteed $4,000 and 50% of entry fees it could make more sense.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA stated that he used to run a lot and never relied
  on the clock. He stated that he had his own timer and that he would start it when he
  began the race and then he would turn it off when he finished. He noted the only
  advantage a chip timer has is that you could be in the back of the group but the
  minute you hit the pad your time is on and that is truly what you gain from a chip.
  He also stated that he asked numerous runners on the course if our mile markers
  were correct as he was concerned since changes to the course were made. He
  explained that the responses he received indicated that runners noted a certain
  marker was two-tenths of a mile off.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted that this is a different race that it is a family
  friendly fun event for our community. He expressed concern that if we start
  introducing chip timing, it may make it more of a competitive feel and is not sure
  that is the ultimate goal.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that she didn’t realize the cost of the chip timers
  and agreed with everything shared by COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA and
  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI. She did note that the City takes pride in the family-
  friendly approach, but the next draw for this event would be for the local mid-level
  runner groups that the chip timing could bring back to this event. She also noted
  that the chips could assist in bringing out a few more awards for the events. ACM
  Davis stated that most local running groups do have an expectation of chip timing,

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
September 19, 2022
   and that the city staff will provide some more information about everything
  discussed as we begin planning for next year’s event.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted that this would be a good event to complete
  a post event survey with the participants.

  C.  TRACY AUSTIN UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief update on sponsors,
  marketing, number of participants, and the typical history of registration with the
  tournament.

  7.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  ROCKBLUFF PLAYGROUND (VERBAL REPORT)

  ACM Davis reported that the playground was installed with the wrong swing set and
  confirmed that the contractor will replace it at no cost to the City. She further
  explained that replacement parts are expected to be installed in December, but until
  then the playground is usable. She also reported that staff is waiting for a quote for
  the additional ADA enhancements needed for the pathway and that staff are
  working with the same sub-contractor.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that he applauds staff’s tenacity in ensuring
  that the contractor covers the cost of the repairs. ACM Davis noted that
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith coordinated the resolution with the
  contractor.

  B.  SOUTH COAST BOTANICAL GARDENS ACTIVITY UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  ACM Davis reported that staff continue to receive communications from the South
  Coast Botanical Garden on their events and provided an overview of the upcoming
  programming and activities that the Garden will be hosting in the upcoming months.
  She explained that the Garden’s new coordinator Stephanie Yinger will be invited
  to come to the Commission quarterly to provide updates.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ asked if the Garden is taking suggestions of programming
  and activities as it might be an opportunity for them to offer information regarding
  toxic plants to horses. ACM Davis stated that she would pass along the information.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
September 19, 2022
   COMMISSIONER RETZ noted that Dapplegray is still looking good. No reported
  issues.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked about the memorial rock at Rockbluff Park.
  ACM Davis and Community Services Supervisor noted that there was a brief
  explanation submitted with the Commission’s weekly update a couple of weeks ago.
  They stated that they would resend the report if needed.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if we could advertise on social media about
  upcoming events months in advance regarding events that we have set dates.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked if there could be an update regarding the
  new events held at Ernie Howlett Park. ACM Davis responded that staff would put
  together a report for the October meeting with a status update.

  C.  PARK CAMERAS (VERBAL REPORT)

  ACM Davis reported that staff received a request from COMMISSIONER
  PERSICHINA about installing park cameras at Ernie Howlett Park. She noted that
  staff have not formally researched park cameras and asked if the Commission is
  interested in staff further studying this option.

  CHAIR CIAROLLA asked if we are mostly concerned about who is on the fields and
  explained that when the cameras were at Chandler Park the equestrians did not
  like it. COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA confirmed this assessment.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA noted that we should be aware of what is going on
  at our parks. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that maybe we should look at
  other parks as well as including Highridge Park. He also noted that we should
  clearly state what the intent is for the cameras. COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA
  noted that it would be expensive. He also stated that recently kids are playing
  soccer as a permitted activity and baseball groups are coming to the park
  unpermitted. He explained that there is an issue with both utilizing the park at the
  same time due to safety concerns. COMMISIONER MCCORMICK stated that he
  was there this past Thursday for a soccer practice and some baseball groups
  approached them saying they spent a lot of money on the fields. He also noted that
  cameras could provide a good security deterrent as well. COMMISSIONER POPE
  noted that she wondered who would be able to look at the camera footage in a
  timely manner to catch any of these issues brought up but agreed that the deterrent
  aspect of the cameras is a great outcome. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI agreed
  that it was a good point made of who would be able to sit and watch that much
  camera footage. COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK stated that if an incident was

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
September 19, 2022
   reported staff could view that date and time of the camera footage.
  COMMISSIONER RETZ stated that we should speak with the City Attorney if we
  place cameras at one park would we need to place cameras at all parks. ACM Davis
  stated that staff would begin the research needed to bring a future update to the
  commission.

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF AUGUST 23, 2022.

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  PERIMETER PATHWAY PROJECT

  ACM Davis stated that there was nothing to report at this time.

  11.  PARK TOURS

  A.  PEPPERWOOD PARK

  The Commission and staff walked through the park.

  B.  PETER WEBER EQUSTRIAN CENTER

  The Commission and staff continued over to the equestrian center where they were
  led through a guided tour of the center by Concession operator, Gil Houle.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI excused himself from the meeting at 7:07 PM.

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR CIAROLLA MOVED TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 7:15 PM TO THE NEXT PARK AND ACTIVITIES
  COMMISSION MEETING ON OCTOBER 17,2022 AT 7:00 P.M., WHICH BE HELD
  AT THE CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBER.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
September 19, 2022
   Respectfully submitted,  Approved,
